title: Do the two answers match?
starter:
let same_f32 (want : float list) (got : float list) : bool =
  false
hints: Check the lengths first, because `List.for_all2` raises when they differ. Then `List.for_all2 (fun a b -> ...) want got` checks every pair.
`a = b` is wrong twice: it says `0.0` equals `-0.0`, and it says a NaN does not equal a NaN. Handle NaN first with `Float.is_nan a && Float.is_nan b`.
For everything else compare the bits: `Int32.bits_of_float a = Int32.bits_of_float b` is true only when all 32 bits agree.
explain: Comparing with `=` asks whether two floats have the same value, which treats `0.0` and `-0.0` as equal and a NaN as unequal to everything. `Int32.bits_of_float` compares the 32 bits instead, and a separate `Float.is_nan` check lets any NaN match any NaN, which is the rule the grader uses for buffers.
